p1_remediation.note: Twenty-seven in-scope P1 findings, plus one P2 (round 17), across twenty-two rounds of Codex/PM review fixed and covered by tests (one further P1, discovered round 9 and filed as UTV2-1662, is out of scope for this lane and tracked separately -- see below). NOTE: round 1's item (2) below (treating any non-true killSwitchNow as drift) was refined by round 14's item (20-21): a genuinely UNREADABLE recheck (null) is now unknown, not a confident parked_drift, unless another signal independently confirms real drift -- round 14 is the current correct behavior. Round 1 (reviewed commit 3bf4174008): (1) readiness-refresh.yml's scheduled job granted only contents/issues permissions; fixed by adding actions:read. (2) verifyKillSwitchesEngagedNow() returns null on query failure but the drift check only rejected the literal false; fixed to treat any non-true result as drift. (3) staleUnknown/stuckRetryable only catch outbox rows stuck past 5m/30m windows; added a broader post-parking-activity check. Round 2 (reviewed commit 0d604843): (4) resolveParkedContractReceipt() queried deploy.yml runs with a server-side status=success filter, blind to a newer non-success run; fixed by fetching the newest run regardless of status. Round 3 (reviewed commit ff0791dc): (5) round-1's fix #3 queried distribution_outbox.updated_at, which apps/api/src/recap-service.ts (a 'parked-enabled' scheduler) also bumps via its own enqueue/markSent calls; fixed by filtering on claimed_at. Round 4 (reviewed commit 414cf0d5): (6) round-3's claimed_at-only check misses a post-parking claim that FAILED (markFailed clears claimed_at); fixed by adding an attempt_count+updated_at signal alongside it. Round 5 (reviewed commit 7cfbf654): (7) round 4's own premise was wrong -- recap-service.ts's recordRecapDeliveryFailure() ALSO calls outbox.markFailed() on a transient Discord failure; replaced the entire outbox-column approach with system_runs.run_type='distribution.process', created exclusively by distribution-worker.ts's claim step. Round 6 (reviewed commit 4cf51766): (8) apps/worker/src/runner.ts's runWorkerCycles reaps stale claims via a SEPARATE step (reapStaleClaims) that creates no system_runs row; fixed with audit_log.action='distribution.reaped_stale_claim'. Round 7 (reviewed commit 84b84a09): (9) the round-6 audit_log write is NOT atomic with the reap mutation (reapStaleClaims resets the row before awaiting audit.record) -- if that write throws, the reap goes undetected; fixed by querying distribution_outbox.last_error (LIKE 'stale claim reaped by%', a new DbFilter 'like' operator added) instead, which the real Supabase-backed reapStaleClaims sets in the SAME atomic UPDATE that clears claimed_at. Round 8 (reviewed commit 2be41dd8): (10) resolveParkedContractReceipt() queried deploy.yml runs filtered to branch:'main', blind to a deploy.yml run manually dispatched from any other branch or tag (workflow_dispatch carries no branches: restriction) that performs the identical production container replacement; fixed by dropping the branch filter so the newest run across every ref is considered, gated by the same pre-existing completed+success check. probeDeploySha's own separate branch:'main' call was deliberately left unchanged -- it answers a different question (deployed SHA vs. main's HEAD specifically). Round 9 (reviewed commit 4e1abf8a): (11) three post-parking activity checks (cycleStartedAt, mergedAt, heartbeatAt vs. receipt.observedAt) compared ISO timestamp strings lexically instead of chronologically -- unsafe when precision differs ('.' sorts before 'Z', so a millisecond-precision timestamp genuinely after a whole-second one could compare as lexically smaller); fixed with an isAfter() helper that parses both sides to epoch millis. (12) worker resume can be invisible to readiness-refresh when the best-effort worker.heartbeat write fails AND every target hits a processing-skip branch (circuit-open/kill-switch/target-disabled) that never reaches processNextDistributionWork; requires changes to apps/worker/src/runner.ts, outside this lane's locked file_scope_lock -- filed as UTV2-1662 for its own lane, not silently dropped. Round 10 (reviewed commit bd4e3ace): (13) GithubReader.latestRun trusted GitHub's default run ordering (by creation time), not by when a run last actually executed -- a manually re-run OLDER run gets another attempt on its SAME run object (bumping updated_at) rather than a new workflow-run entry, and that attempt can still mutate production; a per_page=1 query trusting position 0 would stay blind to that re-execution being the most recent thing that actually touched production; fixed by fetching a bounded page of candidates (per_page=20) and selecting by updated_at via a new, directly-testable selectMostRecentlyUpdatedRun(). Round 11 (reviewed commit 559bb788): (14) the parked-contract receipt is uploaded by deploy.yml's promote job, suffixed with github.run_attempt as of when promote executed -- a failed-jobs-only rerun of a downstream job (smoke, which needs: promote) bumps the run's own run_attempt and updated_at WITHOUT re-running promote or producing a new receipt, so round 10's updated_at-based selection could pick such a run and latestArtifactJson's prefix-only match would fall back to an earlier attempt's stale receipt; fixed by adding run_attempt to WorkflowRun and an optional expectedAttempt parameter to latestArtifactJson, so resolveParkedContractReceipt now requires the receipt to belong to the selected run's own current attempt, treating a mismatch as unavailable rather than trusting a stale attempt. Round 12 (reviewed commit cc95a8f3): (15) a single per_page=20 page could exclude a manually re-run older run entirely if more than 20 newer-by-created_at runs exist; fixed by paginating up to a bounded 5 pages of 100. (16) probeDeploySha trusted a selected run's head_sha directly with no attempt-verification, unlike the parked-receipt path's round-11 check -- a failed-jobs-only rerun of a downstream job (smoke, needs: promote) can advance a run's current attempt without re-running promote; fixed by adding jobConclusionForAttempt() to GithubReader and verifying deploy.yml's promote job (real GitHub display name 'Promote production') succeeded in the selected run's current attempt before trusting its head_sha. Round 13 (reviewed commit 68b1d87d): (17-18) staleUnknown/stuckRetryable (active-mode threshold counters) fed the parked branch's drift detection unbounded, so a row already stuck BEFORE parking would false-trigger PARKED_DRIFT purely by aging past threshold while parked; separately, a live claim whose non-atomic runs.startRun() write failed transiently went undetected during its first 5 minutes; fixed by removing the unbounded counters from the parked branch and replacing them with a single time-scoped liveClaimsSinceParking check (status='processing' AND claimed_at > receipt.observedAt). (19) probeCiVerify shared latestRun's updated_at-based selection, wrong for 'the run for this specific commit' -- an unrelated older ci.yml rerun could shadow a newer, already-passing run for current HEAD; fixed by adding an optional headSha filter (server-side head_sha query param) and having probeCiVerify scope its lookup to the resolved main HEAD. Round 14 (reviewed commit 8bde6b79): (20) probeDeploySha gave up unreadable at the very first candidate when its current attempt hadn't run promote, even though an OLDER candidate's own current attempt genuinely had, discarding a recoverable answer; fixed by adding listRunsByRecency() (the full paginated candidate list, sharing fetchCandidateRuns with latestRun) and walking it past non-promoting attempts to the first genuine deploy. (21) an unreadable kill-switch recheck (killSwitchNow===null) was folded into driftReasons alongside a confirmed false result, producing a false RED (status:'fail', runtime_state:'parked_drift', unreadable_reason:null); fixed by tracking null separately so it downgrades to unknown only when no OTHER signal already proves genuine drift, while a real drift finding from another check still reports fail/parked_drift regardless of kill-switch readability. Round 15 (reviewed commit 3a190143): (22) round 14's fallback-search checked only a candidate's CURRENT attempt for promote, not every attempt -- if promote succeeded in attempt 1 but a later failed-jobs-only rerun of smoke alone created attempt 2 (never re-running promote), round 14 rejected the entire run and fell through to an older, less accurate candidate even though attempt 1's head_sha was still correct; fixed by searching every attempt of a candidate (current down to 1) before moving to the next candidate. (23) apps/ingestor/src/index.ts calls reapStaleRuns() before runIngestorCycles() on every startup, and the real DB implementation updates only status='failed'/finished_at on a stale row, never started_at -- an accidentally-resumed ingestor whose first action is this reap (or that crashes before a first new cycle) left cycleStartedAt reflecting the OLD pre-parking value; fixed by adding a finished_at-after-parking check on ingestor.cycle system_runs rows. Each in-scope fix has a dedicated test asserting the specific failure mode. Two related P2s (30-day artifact retention expiry; explicit image_tag dispatches rejected by the releaseTag===head_sha check) were also flagged but are out of scope for this PR -- tracked separately, not silently dropped. Round 16 (reviewed commit cb0faf40): (24) candidates is ordered by run-level updated_at, which an unrelated downstream job's rerun can bump without touching promote at all -- an OLDER run whose promote succeeded long ago, later given a smoke-only rerun that bumps only its updated_at, would still outrank a genuinely NEWER run whose promote actually completed more recently in real time under rounds 14/15's early-exit-on-first-promoted-candidate selection, reporting the wrong SHA as currently deployed; fixed by having jobConclusionForAttempt return the promote job's own completedAt alongside its conclusion, collecting every candidate whose promote succeeded in any attempt, and selecting the single candidate whose promote job's own completedAt is most recent across the entire set, instead of the first one encountered in updated_at recency order. measured.deploy_run_completed_at and the age/evidence text now report the promote job's own completion time rather than the run's updated_at. Round 17 (reviewed commit 3be07234, P2, no P1s remained): (25) the killSwitchUnreadable branch inside probeWorkerOutboxHealth's parked-mode branch returned the generic unreadable() helper directly, whose measured is always null -- unlike every other unreadable path in this file (both probeIngestorHealth's and probeWorkerOutboxHealth's generic catch blocks), which wrap the result with measured.runtime_state:'unreadable' so a consumer can distinguish an observer failure from active_failed/parked_drift at the field level; fixed to match the established pattern. Round 19-20 (PM review of exact-head 4b2fae0157b2c3f09b7d35c9ca584bd56ade140e; an automated Codex review at the same head returned zero findings first): (26) verifyKillSwitchesEngagedNow() counted rows where killed=false for best-bets/trader-insights and returned true (engaged) when both counts were zero -- a MISSING target row also produces a zero count for that query, so an absent delivery_kill_switch record could be silently certified as engaged, defeating the entire parked_verified contract's dependence on kill switches actually being confirmed. Fixed by requiring, per required target, exactly one row (countRows on the target alone) AND that row's own killed column reads strictly true (latestRow); missing, duplicate, or malformed evidence all now fail closed identically to an unreadable query. Three new tests cover a missing target row, duplicate target rows, and a malformed (null) killed value. Two accompanying governance findings were also remediated: Branch Discipline (three old commit messages referenced UTV2-1640/1647/1662 alongside UTV2-1660) was fixed by squashing the branch's full history to a clean UTV2-1660-only commit set; File Scope Lock (readiness-refresh.yml added after the trusted first-commit scope snapshot) was resolved as a side effect of that same squash -- the new first commit's lane manifest declares the complete final file list, confirmed green on CI with no manual scope-override needed. Round 21 (fresh Codex review of exact-head 11dcc7ce): (27) probeDeploySha's listRunsByRecency call passed status:'success' straight through to GitHub's REST API as a server-side filter on the run's OVERALL conclusion -- a run where promote itself succeeds (mutating production) but a later, unrelated downstream job (smoke) fails turns the whole workflow run's conclusion to failure, so that run would never even appear in candidates, silently hiding a genuine production mutation from the pre-existing per-attempt promote-job check. Fixed by dropping the status filter entirely; every run on main is now a candidate, and only jobConclusionForAttempt(promote) decides trust, never the run's own aggregate status/conclusion fields. New regression test proves a run stubbed with conclusion:'failure' overall is still trusted as the deployed SHA when its own promote job succeeded. Round 22 (PM review of exact-head 192b597d): (30) countRows() selected a hardcoded 'id' column for every table -- delivery_kill_switch has no id column at all (schema: actor, killed, reason, target, updated_at), so every real call against it failed at the PostgREST level, always falling through to unreadable; this bug predates round 20, just never exercised against a real client in any test. Fixed by adding an optional countColumn parameter (default 'id' for backward compat on every other call site), passing 'target' explicitly for delivery_kill_switch. New test goes through wrapReadOnlyClient with a fake reader that genuinely rejects a nonexistent column, not just a dictionary stub. (31) probeDeploySha trusted the 'Promote production' JOB's own conclusion as proof of a production mutation -- but the job runs its health-check loop and any rollback in steps AFTER the actual container-replacement step, in the same job, so a later health-check failure marked the whole job failed even when the mutation had already genuinely occurred; worse, a successful rollback left production running a DIFFERENT tag entirely, which job-conclusion-based trust could never express. Fixed with a new durable-evidence mechanism in deploy.yml's promote job: a deploy-mutation-receipt artifact is written and uploaded immediately after the container-replacement step succeeds, independent of the health-check/rollback step's outcome; a deploy-rollback-receipt artifact records a successful rollback as a separate, newer mutation to a different tag. probeDeploySha now selects trust and the deployed tag purely from these artifacts' presence and timestamps, never any job's conclusion; jobConclusionForAttempt and DEPLOY_PROMOTE_JOB_NAME were removed as dead code. Every deploy-alignment test was rewritten onto the new mechanism, plus three new tests for mutation-succeeded/health-failed/no-rollback, mutation-succeeded/health-failed/rollback-succeeded (rollback tag wins), and failure-before-mutation (no evidence, falls through cleanly).

mutation_verification.note: Dedicated new tests each assert a distinct behavior that would silently regress if the corresponding logic were removed: parked_verified is reported (not active_healthy) when parked evidence is confirmed and no post-parking activity exists; parked_drift fires on a post-parking ingestor cycle, a post-parking worker heartbeat, a receipt autorun-flag mismatch, and a kill-switch re-check that disagrees with the receipt's own claim; the exact pre-existing active-mode branch (same thresholds, same failure strings) is exercised verbatim when the parked receipt cannot be resolved (no successful deploy run) or when the releaseTag doesn't match the run's head SHA.

runtime_proof.production_diagnostic: No production mutation performed. This lane only changes how readiness-refresh.ts interprets already-public deploy.yml receipts and adds a same-run artifact upload to deploy.yml; it does not change deploy.yml's release/promotion/rollback logic in any way.

blast_radius.note: Merging performs no production mutation. deploy.yml's confirm-step change only ADDS a receipt-file write + artifact upload after the existing confirm logic already succeeded or failed; it does not alter any release, promotion, or rollback behavior. readiness-refresh.ts's change only affects how the next scheduled/dispatched readiness-refresh run classifies the ingestor_health/worker_outbox_health dimensions; it cannot make a genuinely active-and-failing service read as parked_verified, since parked_verified requires an independently-fetched, releaseTag-bound receipt whose own mode field says "parked".
